title: Votes for women
examples: What was the main difference between the suffragists and the suffragettes?
When exactly did women gain the right to vote in the UK?
What kind of protests did the suffragettes use?

explain.say: Today we are learning about the fight for women's right to vote.
Some women believed in peaceful ways to gain the vote.
Other women used more direct and sometimes dramatic actions.
The year nineteen eighteen was a major turning point for women's rights.
By nineteen twenty eight, the fight for full voting equality was achieved.
Imagine a modern election where women's voices are finally heard.

faq.q: Why did the movement split into two groups?
faq.a: The movement split because some women preferred peaceful methods while others felt more direct action was necessary. This is similar to how people sometimes disagree on the best way to solve a problem. You might also ask: What was the difference between the two groups? Or: Why were there two sides?
asks: What was the difference between the suffragists and suffragettes?

faq.a: Suffrage simply means the right to vote in elections. Before this movement, only certain groups of people could vote. You might also ask: What is the right to vote? Or: What does suffrage mean?
asks: What does it mean to have the right to vote?

faq.q: Was getting the vote an instant event?
faq.a: No, it was a long and difficult struggle over many years. The movement involved many different strategies over decades. You might also ask: How long did it take? Or: Was it quick?
asks: How long did the fight last?
Did they get it all at once?

faq.q: What kind of actions did the suffragettes take?
faq.a: The suffragettes were known for more militant actions, such as disruptive protests and civil disobedience. These actions were designed to gain public and political attention. You might also ask: What did they do? Or: Were they peaceful?
asks: What were the suffragettes known for?

faq.a: The year 1918 marked a significant step, granting voting rights to some women. This was a partial victory in the long struggle. You might also ask: What happened in 1918? Or: Was 1918 the end?
asks: Did they get all the votes in 1918?

facts: Suffragists generally advocated for peaceful methods of gaining the vote.
Suffragettes were known for more militant and direct forms of protest. This was a key difference.
The year 1918 granted voting rights to some women in the United Kingdom.
Full voting equality for women in the UK was achieved by 1928.

quiz.say: Which group focused primarily on peaceful lobbying and marches?
quiz.why: The suffragists were known for their constitutional and peaceful methods of campaigning.

wrong.1: The suffragettes were known for more confrontational and direct actions.
wrong.2: Parliament was the place where the laws were debated, not the group protesting.
wrong.3: 1918 was a date marking a partial victory, not the group itself.

quiz.say: If a group used civil disobedience to gain attention, they were more like which group?
quiz.why: The suffragettes were the group associated with more militant and disruptive forms of protest.

wrong.1: The suffragists preferred working through established, peaceful political channels.
wrong.2: 1928 is the year of full rights, not the group doing the action.
wrong.3: A peaceful march is a method, not the name of the group.

quiz.say: Which date marks the point where women achieved full voting rights in the UK?
quiz.why: The year 1928 signifies the point when women gained full voting equality.

wrong.0: 1918 was only a partial victory, not the final goal.
wrong.1: This is a group name, not a year.
wrong.2: This is a place name, not the specific date.
